# Higher-order beta-(2,1) clock-reset family generated by the beta stabilizer

**Status:** EXACT CHARACTER/SLOPE ALGEBRA + EXACT-ENVELOPE DESIGN FAMILY + FROZEN PRINCIPAL POLARIZATION AUDIT FOR ONE REPRESENTATIVE. NOT YET A COMPLETE ACTIVE RESET CELL. This note replaces the obsolete idea that the beta-(2,1) cell must renew at the first turning-point return. The beta-preserving lattice stabilizer supplies an infinite family of higher-order target generator pairs which, if physically promoted by the nonlinear genealogy, return exactly to the original beta-two/beta-one slope coordinates at a later non-turning section. For suitable finite parameters the spent old catalyst is then exponentially below the renewed beta-two parent, eliminating the terminal old-`C` cleanup problem.

The representative `(u,n,delta)=(15,7,0.035)` passes the exact action-root and principal polarization tests, but its full intermediate critical audit is large. It is therefore a proof-of-mechanism/design candidate, not the final selected cell.

## 1. Beta-preserving stabilizer and physical target characters

Use the two old unit-beta generators `C,D` and the beta-two parent

\[
P=C+D.
\]

Put

\[
M:=D-C,\qquad \beta(M)=0.
\]

The beta vector for `(P,C)` is `(2,1)^T`. Its orientation-preserving stabilizer contains

\[
U_n
=I+n\begin{pmatrix}2\\1\end{pmatrix}(1,-2)
=
\begin{pmatrix}
1+2n&-4n\\
n&1-2n
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad n\in\mathbb Z.
\tag{HC1}
\]

Since

\[
U_n(2,1)^T=(2,1)^T,
\]

the transformed generator characters again have beta weights `(2,1)`. Rewriting them in the `(C,D)` basis gives the physical target pair

\[
\boxed{
C_n=nD-(n-1)C
=D+(n-1)M,
}
\tag{HC2}
\]

and

\[
\boxed{
P_n=(2n+1)D-(2n-1)C
=2D+(2n-1)M.
}
\tag{HC3}
\]

Thus the lattice stabilizer is not being used as a mere relabelling: the programme target is to **physically promote** the characters (HC2)--(HC3) through a finite mean-root genealogy.

For `n=1`,

\[
C_1=D,
\qquad
P_1=3D-C,
\]

which is the previously studied strong-`H` renewal. Higher `n` continue the same beta-zero root direction.

## 2. General non-turning relay geometry

Drop the obsolete passive-cleanup gauge `x+delta=1`. Keep only the exact first relay resonance

\[
\boxed{
\mathcal E_{2,u}(x)
=
\mathcal E_{1,u}(x+\delta)
+
\mathcal E_{1,u}(x-\delta).
}
\tag{HC4}
\]

At offset `t`, the old unit-beta slopes are

\[
z_C(t)=x+\delta+t,
\qquad
z_D(t)=x-\delta+t.
\tag{HC5}
\]

The beta-zero root changes only the beta-weighted radial coefficient, so the target reduced slopes are

\[
\boxed{
z_{C_n}(t)=x-(2n-1)\delta+t,}
\tag{HC6}
\]

\[
\boxed{
z_{P_n}(t)=x-2n\delta+t.}
\tag{HC7}
\]

Choose the clock-reset section

\[
\boxed{T_n:=2n\delta.}
\tag{HC8}
\]

Then exactly

\[
\boxed{z_{P_n}(T_n)=x,}
\tag{HC9}
\]

and

\[
\boxed{z_{C_n}(T_n)=x+\delta.}
\tag{HC10}
\]

Therefore the physically promoted pair `(P_n,C_n)` returns to precisely the same beta-two/beta-one slope coordinates as the original `(P,C)` bank, without requiring either channel to lie at a turning point.

This is the fundamental higher-order clock-reset identity.

## 3. Exact action-renewal equations

The absolute-leaf action of `C_n=nD-(n-1)C` at a generation section `t_c` is

\[
n\mathcal E_{1,u}(x-\delta+t_c)
+(n-1)\mathcal E_{1,u}(x+\delta+t_c).
\]

Exact source-envelope matching to the natural beta-one target requires

\[
\boxed{
F_{C_n}(t_c)
:=
n\mathcal E_{1,u}(x-\delta+t_c)
+(n-1)\mathcal E_{1,u}(x+\delta+t_c)
-\mathcal E_{1,u}(x-(2n-1)\delta+t_c)
=0.
}
\tag{HC11}
\]

Likewise `P_n=(2n+1)D-(2n-1)C` has exact action-renewal equation

\[
\boxed{
F_{P_n}(t_p)
:=
(2n+1)\mathcal E_{1,u}(x-\delta+t_p)
+(2n-1)\mathcal E_{1,u}(x+\delta+t_p)
-\mathcal E_{2,u}(x-2n\delta+t_p)
=0.
}
\tag{HC12}
\]

If roots

\[
0<t_p,t_c<T_n
\]

exist, then homogeneous propagation to `T_n` gives exactly

\[
A_{P_n}(T_n)=\mathcal E_{2,u}(x),
\qquad
A_{C_n}(T_n)=\mathcal E_{1,u}(x+\delta).
\tag{HC13}
\]

Thus the renewed pair reproduces the original natural action levels as well as the slope coordinates.

## 4. Passive disposal of the old catalyst

The old catalyst, if simply propagated to `T_n`, has slope

\[
\boxed{z_C^{old}(T_n)=x+(2n+1)\delta.}
\tag{HC14}
\]

and action

\[
A_C^{old}(T_n)
=\mathcal E_{1,u}(x+(2n+1)\delta).
\]

Define the higher-order cleanup defect relative to the renewed beta-two parent by

\[
\boxed{
\Delta_{clean}^{(n)}
:=
\mathcal E_{1,u}(x+(2n+1)\delta)
-
\mathcal E_{2,u}(x).
}
\tag{HC15}
\]

If

\[
\Delta_{clean}^{(n)}<0,
\]

then the spent old catalyst is exponentially below the renewed parent on the source action scale and requires no terminal cancellation gate.

Unlike the old `n=1`, `x+delta=1` turning construction, the new boundary may satisfy

\[
\mathcal E_{1,u}(x+\delta)<0,
\]

so every additional surviving `D` leaf costs a fixed negative action and the zero-cost infinite ladder from `beta21_turning_face_zero_cost_ladder_obstruction.md` disappears.

## 6. A finite spanning genealogy and polarization nonvanishing

A convenient spanning genealogy is

\[
M
\to D+M
\to\cdots\to D+6M=C_7,
\tag{HC29}
\]

then

\[
(D+6M)+D\to2D+6M,
\tag{HC30}
\]

followed by

\[
2D+6M
\to2D+7M
\to\cdots\to2D+13M=P_7.
\tag{HC31}
\]

At the frozen `u=15` representative every mandatory principal coefficient is far from zero.

At the parent-generation section `t=t_{P_7}`, the six mean-wave edges in (HC29) have approximate coefficients

\[
-34.72,-35.11,-35.57,-36.13,-36.80,-37.65,
\]

the wave-wave bridge (HC30) has coefficient approximately

\[
+3.47,
\]

and the seven beta-two mean-root steps in (HC31) lie between approximately

\[
-65.88\quad\text{and}\quad-68.20.
\]

At `t=t_{C_7}` the corresponding ranges are approximately

\[
-37.54\text{ to }-40.02,
\qquad
+3.09,
\qquad
-71.43\text{ to }-73.34.
\]

Thus

\[
\boxed{
\min |\kappa_{edge}|>3
}
\tag{HC32}
\]

for the entire displayed spanning genealogy at both diagnostic sections. No polarization zero appears on this route.

## 7. Why this is not yet the selected final design

The representative (HC16) solves the terminal problems cleanly, but it creates a new finite-complexity issue upstream.

At the beta-two parent-generation section, both old unit-beta parents are close to their own turning regions. A crude maximal absolute-leaf audit therefore contains a large number of naturally critical and positive-defect lattice characters. The same phenomenon, though less severe, appears at the later catalyst section.

This does **not** by itself prove an obstruction:

- maximal absolute-leaf bookkeeping overcounts unreachable genealogies;
- same-phase self-interactions vanish;
- polarization zeros and causal generation order remove additional rows;
- the infinite stable complement still has smoothing.

But it means that this representative should not be promoted directly to an exact `C^1` gate theorem before a full reachable-genealogy audit.

Accordingly `(15,7,0.035)` is retained as a **mechanism certificate**, not as the final optimized working point.

## 8. Correct optimization problem

A viable final higher-order design should minimize not only terminal cleanup but the complete active-control complexity. For each candidate `(u,n,delta,x,t_P,t_C)` require:

1. exact relay resonance (HC4);
2. causal roots of (HC11)--(HC12);
3. source-window margins for both generated target slopes;
4. fixed negative terminal cleanup defect (HC15);
5. fixed nonzero polarization margins on a sufficient genealogy;
6. negative old-parent actions at every generation section;
7. as small as possible a **reachable** positive-defect block at both generator events;
8. positive width margins preserving that classification.

The next computational/theorem layer must therefore optimize by reachable critical-block size, not merely by `Delta_clean`.

## 9. Programme consequence

The turning-face obstruction is not a no-go theorem for beta-(2,1) active renewal. The higher-order stabilizer provides a concrete alternative:

\[
\boxed{
(P,C)
\rightsquigarrow
(P_n,C_n)
\quad\text{with}\quad
(\beta,slope)_{out}=(\beta,slope)_{in},
}
\tag{HC33}
\]

where the new characters are physically generated and the old catalyst can be action-subcritical at the handoff.

The outstanding question is now finite-dimensional complexity of the higher-order promotion, not phase-clock renewal or terminal old-`C` cleanup.
